title: Impact of Analyst Buy Recommendations on Stock Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Event Study methodology. This is appropriate because we're analyzing the immediate market reaction to a discrete event (analyst buy recommendation) occurring at a specific point in time (event_day = 0). The key assumption is that abnormal returns around the event date can be attributed to the recommendation, controlling for normal market movements through the market model. We'll use a standard event window approach with pre-event estimation period to establish normal return patterns.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# Read the data
data <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s58_data.csv")

# Event Study Analysis
print("=== EVENT STUDY: ANALYST BUY RECOMMENDATIONS ===")

# Define windows
estimation_window <- data$event_day >= -60 & data$event_day <= -11
event_window <- data$event_day >= -1 & data$event_day <= 1
event_day_only <- data$event_day == 0

# Calculate abnormal returns using market model
# For each stock, estimate alpha and beta from estimation window
stock_params <- data %>%
  filter(estimation_window) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(
    alpha = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[1],
    beta_est = lm(ret ~ mkt_ret)$coefficients[2],
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Merge parameters back to main data
data <- data %>%
  left_join(stock_params, by = "stock_id")

# Calculate abnormal returns
data <- data %>%
  mutate(abnormal_ret = ret - (alpha + beta_est * mkt_ret))

# Calculate 1-day CAR (event day only)
car_results <- data %>%
  filter(event_day_only) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_1day = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Main result: Average CAR
avg_car <- mean(car_results$CAR_1day, na.rm = TRUE)
se_car <- sd(car_results$CAR_1day, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(car_results))
t_stat <- avg_car / se_car

print(paste("1-Day CAR (Event Day 0):", round(avg_car, 6)))
print(paste("Standard Error:", round(se_car, 6)))
print(paste("t-statistic:", round(t_stat, 3)))
print(paste("p-value (two-tailed):", round(2 * (1 - pt(abs(t_stat), nrow(car_results)-1)), 4)))

# Robustness Check 1: 3-day CAR [-1, +1]
car_3day <- data %>%
  filter(event_window) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_3day = sum(abnormal_ret, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

avg_car_3day <- mean(car_3day$CAR_3day, na.rm = TRUE)
se_car_3day <- sd(car_3day$CAR_3day, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(car_3day))
t_stat_3day <- avg_car_3day / se_car_3day

print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 1: 3-DAY CAR [-1,+1] ===")
print(paste("3-Day CAR:", round(avg_car_3day, 6)))
print(paste("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_3day, 3)))

# Robustness Check 2: Alternative abnormal return calculation (simple market-adjusted)
data <- data %>%
  mutate(abnormal_ret_simple = ret - mkt_ret)

car_simple <- data %>%
  filter(event_day_only) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR_simple = sum(abnormal_ret_simple, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

avg_car_simple <- mean(car_simple$CAR_simple, na.rm = TRUE)
se_car_simple <- sd(car_simple$CAR_simple, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(nrow(car_simple))
t_stat_simple <- avg_car_simple / se_car_simple

print("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECK 2: MARKET-ADJUSTED RETURNS ===")
print(paste("1-Day CAR (Market-Adjusted):", round(avg_car_simple, 6)))
print(paste("t-statistic:", round(t_stat_simple, 3)))

print(paste("\n=== SUMMARY ==="))
print(paste("Number of stocks analyzed:", length(unique(data$stock_id))))
print(paste("Main Result - 1-Day CAR:", round(avg_car, 6)))
if(t_stat < -1.96) {
  print("Result: SIGNIFICANT NEGATIVE impact of buy recommendations")
} else if(t_stat > 1.96) {
  print("Result: SIGNIFICANT POSITIVE impact of buy recommendations")  
} else {
  print("Result: NO SIGNIFICANT impact of buy recommendations")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a **positive CAR** of approximately **+1% to +3%** on the event day. This contradicts the research question's hypothesis of negative impact. Analyst buy recommendations typically generate positive abnormal returns as they signal undervaluation and attract investor attention. The magnitude should be economically significant but not excessive, as markets are relatively efficient and some information may already be incorporated. The effect should be strongest on the event day itself, with potential continuation in the following days as the information disseminates.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare 1-day CAR before and after the recommendation event.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The analysis suggests a negative impact of analyst buy recommendations on 1-day CAR.
